title: Srinagar MP Ruhullah Mehdi quits National Conference and Lok Sabha over Article 370
dek: He accuses Omar Abdullah's party of dropping its promise to fight for special status. NC leaders call his exit an 'Operation Lotus' and point to remarks by the BJP's Ram Madhav.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Srinagar's MP, Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, has quit the National Conference (NC), the party that governs Jammu and Kashmir, and resigned his Lok Sabha seat, accusing its leaders of abandoning their promise to fight for the restoration of Article 370. The NC hit back on Wednesday, calling his exit an "Operation Lotus", a phrase used for alleged attempts by the BJP to break opposition parties.

Mehdi announced his decision on Tuesday, 3 November, before a gathering of supporters at Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam on the 26th death anniversary of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi. In a letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla dated 3 November, which he posted on X, he wrote that "in exercise of the right conferred by Article 101(3)(b) of the Constitution of India", he was resigning his seat "with immediate effect", one report said. The resignation takes effect once the Speaker accepts it; the seat would then fall vacant and a by-election would have to be held.

## Why he left

Mehdi, a three-time MLA from Budgam whom the NC's spokesman called "an important religious personality", won Srinagar for the NC in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. His office said the party had sought power on promises to restore Article 370, release prisoners and protect people's rights. "They sought power on those promises, then treated us as fools for expecting them to deliver," the statement said. "There is no fixing this rot from within."

He told reporters that people had come to the gathering on their own "for the sake of principles", and hinted at building a new political movement, saying he would not involve leaders "who have baggage". He set no timeline.

The rift had been growing for more than a year, one report said. Mehdi led a protest in Srinagar against the reservation policy soon after the NC formed the government in late 2024, and accused party leaders of betraying voters at a working committee meeting in May 2025. Earlier this year NC president Farooq Abdullah challenged him to resign and fight a fresh election. "I challenge him to resign as an MP and face the election. We will see who votes for him," Abdullah said, according to that report.

## The NC's response

NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar said on Tuesday that the party had hoped Mehdi would reconsider and that differences "could have been resolved through dialogue".

On Wednesday the tone hardened. NC legislator Sajad Shaheen compared the episode to 1953, when party founder Sheikh Abdullah was arrested, and 1984, when the party split, and asked whether a statement about Mehdi by BJP national vice-president Ram Madhav was "a coincidence", one report said. Another NC MLA, Salman Sagar, rejected Mehdi's charge that the party had dropped Articles 370 and 35A. "It will be a political suicide to abandon Article 370 and 35A," he said. Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary said Ram Madhav's remarks were "proof" that Mehdi was working under the BJP's direction.

The BJP has not publicly responded to the NC's accusation. Mehdi has said his opposition is rooted in unfulfilled promises, not in any demand for office.

## Pressure inside the NC

The resignation comes as Chief Minister Omar Abdullah faces discontent within his own ranks. One report said that more than a dozen NC legislators met in Srinagar after four new ministers were sworn in, and expressed unhappiness with the Cabinet expansion. Sagar said the party would address the matter "within two to three days".

## What happens next

The Speaker must accept the resignation before the Election Commission can schedule a by-election for Srinagar, which the Representation of the People Act generally requires within six months of a seat falling vacant.
